subject: Request: temporary SLA grace for throughput degradation during migration
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit@fastlytech.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@fastlytech.com, ops@fastlytech.com
Date: 2026-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: sustained throughput degradation — request for temporary SLA grace and updated escalation path

Hi Tessa / Sean,

We started seeing a sustained throughput degradation across our production traffic to Redwood (in us-west) starting ~02:00 PT this morning. Token latency is spiking and tails are worse than the 99th percentile guarantees we have in the current SLO. Our infra team is migrating routing for a regional cache cluster this weekend which we believe is contributing to intermittent KV cache misses and slower token retrieval.

We need to request a short, formal exception to the P1/P2 response commitments for the migration window (estimated 36 hours). Specifically: a temporary grace on P2 response SLA (allow P2 responses up to 4 hours) and confirmation that P1/incident routing and escalation paths remain prioritized. We also want a clear mutual action plan (who owns what, on-call contacts, and communications cadence).

Attached: fastly-prod-incident-log-0529.txt (snippets).

Can Redwood confirm:
- Whether you can accept a time-bounded SLA adjustment for P2 only (36 hours, starting 2026-05-29 02:00 PT)
- Primary and secondary on-call contacts and escalation ladder during the window
- Any runbook steps we should follow to reduce impact

Appreciate a quick reply — we may need to escalate to procurement if a formal amendment / credit is required.

Thanks,
Amit
Head of Platform Engineering
FastlyTech
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@fastlytech.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, contracts@fastlytech.com
Date: 2026-05-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained throughput degradation — request for temporary SLA grace and updated escalation path

Hi Amit — thanks for the details and the log. We're on this. Quick answers up front: we can do a time-limited P2 grace for the migration window, and we will keep P1 handling at our highest priority (immediate paging and 30-minute acknowledgement). That said, we need internal sign-off for the commercial/contractual amendment and a short mutual action plan.

Proposed immediate plan:
- Acceptable temporary SLA: P2 response time relaxed to 4 hours for the window 2026-05-29 02:00 PT through 2026-05-30 14:00 PT (36 hours).
- P1 handling: remain unchanged — on-call will page and acknowledge within 30 minutes; escalation to SRE lead if not resolved in 60 minutes.
- On-call coverage: Primary: Irene Choi (SRE) 24/7; Secondary: Marissa Cole (Product Ops) daytime; Tertiary: Sean Gallagher (AE) for customer comms.
- Communications cadence: 2x daily status (10:30 PT / 16:30 PT) + ad-hoc for P1 pages.
- Commercial: Ben will propose a one-time service credit if this materially violates production guarantees.

Irene — tagging you for technical confirmation and to attach the mitigation runbook. Ben — can you confirm commercial language we should offer FastlyTech? Marissa — can you own the canary/monitoring dashboard link and the external status updates?

I'll get a draft SLA amendment out if we agree, and we can DocuSign for signatures to make it formal.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit@fastlytech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-29T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained throughput degradation — request for temporary SLA grace and updated escalation path

Thanks, Tessa + Amit. Quick technical note and proposed mitigations (short list):
- Root cause hypothesis: regional cache migration causing KV cache miss amplification and higher token fetch times.
- Immediate mitigations:
  1) Temporary request-level prefix caching on our edge tier for FastlyTech keys — reduces KV calls for common prefixes (risk: slightly stale completions for pinned keys).
  2) Throttle background compaction jobs during migration window to free CPU for inference processes.
  3) Hold low-priority background batching (analytics) to preserve GPU headroom.
- Operational changes to SLA handling:
  - P1: page SRE rotation immediately, acknowledge within 30 minutes. Our SRE runbook will prioritize incident containment and rollback to previous routing if latency fails SLO thresholds for 30m sustained.
  - P2: change to 4-hour response for the window. P2 tickets still routed to on-call but deprioritized behind critical P1 pages.

I've attached a short runbook (sre-action-plan-0529.pdf) with steps we'll execute. We can implement the prefix caching in ~45-90 minutes once you greenlight; rolling back is straightforward.

If FastlyTech is comfortable with the temporary tradeoffs (possible slight increase in token duplication for pinned prefixes), we'll proceed. We'll also share monitoring links for the specific keys you're concerned about.

Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: sre-action-plan-0529.pdf]
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@fastlytech.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@fastlytech.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-29T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained throughput degradation — request for temporary SLA grace and updated escalation path

Amit — thanks for raising this and thanks team for the quick coordination. From a commercial standpoint we can offer:
- A one-time service credit equal to 7% of May 2026 hosted usage for FastlyTech if we confirm the degradation was caused by Redwood's routing changes/behaviors. If the root cause is on FastlyTech's migration/config, we will still prioritise remediation but we'd reserve credit discussion.
- We will prepare a 1-page SLA amendment that notes the temporary P2 grace window, the unchanged P1 commitments, and the credit clause (conditional).

I've attached an initial draft SLA amendment (SLA-Amendment-Draft-FastlyTech-0529.pdf). If that looks good we can route via DocuSign (link below) for an official amendment.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC12345
Redwood amendment preview: https://app.redwood.inference.com/agreements/DL-7492/amendment

Please confirm you want us to proceed with the prefix-caching mitigation (Irene), and whether you accept the proposed P2 4-hour window. If you accept, we'll get the amendment signed and have operations execute.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA-Amendment-Draft-FastlyTech-0529.pdf]

Team — thanks for the fast turn. FastlyTech accepts the proposed technical mitigations and the temporary P2 4-hour window for the 36-hour period you specified. We also accept the DocuSign flow for the one-page amendment; we'll review the SLA draft and sign once Ben drops the final.

Please proceed with prefix caching and throttling background jobs. We'll keep our end on monitoring and will escalate immediately if we hit a P1. Also please send the two scheduled status updates (10:30 / 16:30 PT) and link to the dashboard.

Amit
Head of Platform Engineering
FastlyTech
